title: Maple Brown Sugar Cookies with Maple Icing
creator: Okkleeek
servings: Not specified (creator made larger cookies; size flexible)
prepTime: Not specified (plus chill at least 3 hours, ideally overnight)
ingredients: 2⅓ cups (292g) all-purpose flour, spooned and levelled
½ cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened to room temperature
Maple icing (optional): ⅓ cup (80ml) pure maple syrup
Maple icing (optional): 1 cup (112g) sifted confectioners' sugar
Maple icing (optional): Pinch of salt, to taste
instructions: Step 1: Whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Step 2: In a separate bowl, cream the softened butter and brown sugar until combined. Mix in the egg and maple syrup.
Step 3: Gradually add the dry ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
Step 4: Cover and chill the dough for at least 3 hours, or ideally overnight. The dough is naturally sticky because of the maple syrup, so chilling is important.

Step 5: Once chilled, let the dough sit out briefly to soften just enough to work with. Divide into portions and roll into balls, handling the dough as little as possible. Make them whatever size you prefer.
Step 6: Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 12–13 minutes, or until the edges are set. Allow the cookies to cool.

Step 7: For the icing, melt the butter and maple syrup together in a saucepan. Remove from the heat, then whisk in the sifted confectioners' sugar and a pinch of salt until smooth. Drizzle over the cooled cookies.
notes: From an Okkleeek Facebook reel captioned 'Maple brown sugar cookies with maple icing.' Full recipe is in the public caption (cookie ingredients, optional maple icing, instructions, and tips). Soft, buttery, chewy maple cookies meant as a cozy fall bake.
